criteria.evidence: Tomorrow step 1: "Disable scheduling on cmp-12 (state-changing): openstack compute service set --disable --disable-reason "DIMM replacement" cmp-12 nova-compute". This comes before the DB, GPU and ordinary VM moves.

criteria.criterion: Includes post-repair verification and re-enable step
criteria.evidence: Step 8 checks the host: full memory size, ECC errors clear, nova-compute and agents up. Step 10: "Re-enable the compute service (state-changing). Optionally boot a test instance first."

criteria.criterion: Labels steps read-only vs state-changing or otherwise marks state changes needing approval
criteria.evidence: Steps carry *Read-only* or *(state-changing)* labels throughout. Closing note: "State-changing steps above require approval by the accountable owner".

Mentions evacuation only to warn against it: "Don't use evacuation. Evacuation is for failed hosts... it would risk two copies of the same VM."

summary: The response passes all six criteria and commits none of the three critical errors. It disables nova-compute first and treats the GPU passthrough VMs as cold-migrate or downtime only. It flags the in-memory DB as a live-migration risk and leaves that decision to the DB owner. It verifies each move and that the host is empty before power-off, checks the host after the repair, then re-enables the service. State-changing steps are labelled and need owner approval. There are no book citations, and the environment details it gives (for example \"about 17 (assumed)\") are marked as assumptions, not presented as known facts.
